JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental case: Q1 2026 delivered the strongest quarterly results in available history with revenue of $49.84B (+10.0% YoY), EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY), and net income of $16.49B (+12.6% YoY). Operating margin expanded to 41.1% and ROE improved to 16.2%. The franchise is best-in-class — #1 on Forbes Global 2000 for four consecutive years, top investment bank by fees for 17 straight years ($9.6B in 2025), with structural diversification across consumer, investment banking, commercial, and asset management segments. Valuation sits at the lower-middle of its 12-month range: P/E of 15.5x (range 13.7x–17.8x) and P/B of 2.5x (range 2.2x–2.8x) despite the earnings acceleration, offering a 6.5% earnings yield with a +210bp spread over the 10-year Treasury. The near-term catalyst stack is credible: stress-test passage on 2026-06-25 triggered a 10% dividend hike and $50B buyback authorization; European digital banking expansion into France, Italy, and Spain announced 2026-06-16; and a strengthening capital-markets pipeline (SpaceX IPO fees, upcoming OpenAI/Anthropic IPOs). Macro conditions are constructive with a mildly positive yield curve (T10Y2Y=0.31%), VIX collapsed from 30.6 to 18.9, and rates in the 3.75%–4.25% sweet spot for bank NII. Morningstar forecasts NII growth of 8.7% in 2026. Offsetting factors include expense guidance creep to ~$106B, a DOJ debanking probe, and the stock already +13.4% over the past quarter within 2.4% of its 365-day high. These limit the score below +0.5 but the multi-factor fundamental and valuation case supports a solidly constructive rating.
